To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

chronic administration of glucocorticoids to rats causes a rapid accumulation of osmiophilic particles in the smooth endoplamic reticulum and Golgi complex of hepatocytes, which are consistent with the increased synthesis and secretion of lipoprotein particles.
the effects of glucocorticoids on hepatic structure are consistent with a mechanism of action that involves an increased secretion of very low density lipoproteins.

chronic dexamethsone administration to male rats caused an accumulation of osmiophilic particles in hepatocytes, and that these particles were associated with the smooth endoplamic reticulum, the Golgi apparatus, and secretory vesicles.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of DEX on hepatic ultrastructural organization.
the mechanisms by which glucocorticoids alter hepatic ultrastructure, plasma lipoprotein metabolism, and carbohydrate metabolism.
the effects of glucocorticoids on the synthesis and secretion of lipoproteins and on glycogen metabolism in the liver.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

chronic DEX administration causes a change in the distribution of glycogen particles in the hepatocytes, an increase in the number of SER membranes, an increase in SER membrane‐associated osmiophilic particles and a decrease in the number of mitochondria per unit volume of cytoplasm.
chronic administration of dexamethasome causes alterations in hepatic ultrastructure that are consistent with an increase in the synthesis and secretion of lipoproteins.
the administration of glucocorticoids causes the liver cell to respond by altering its fine structure in a manner that is consistent with the synthesis of lipoproteins.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the effects of chronic DEX administration on hepatic fine structure are consistent with a role of the SER in lipoprotein secretion.
the administration of DEX to rats results in a rapid and transient accumulation of lipoproteins in the plasma and a more prolonged accumulation of lipoprotein precursors within the hepatocyte.

the administration of DEX to rats results in an increase in the amount of SER in the cell, a change in the association of glycogenic particles with SER, an increase in the synthesis of VLDL in hepatocytes and an increase in plasma lipoprotein concentration.
The main takeaway from our work is that
DEX‐induced alterations in hepatic ultrastructure are associated with the elevation of VLDL levels and the accumulation of glycogen in the hepatocyte.

DEX‐treatment causes a rapid accumulation of lipoproteins in the hepatocyte, a process that involves the SER and the Golgi apparatus, and that this accumulation is accompanied by a change in the distribution of glycogen particles in the hepatocyte.
the effects of glucocorticoids on the liver are not limited to the induction of enzymes involved in the synthesis of VLDL.
